subject: radiology
title: TIPS technique: puncture to patency

steps.tx: Technique starts at the neck, because jugular access gives a straight highway toward the liver veins. **Right jugular access** under ultrasound guides a sheath down the cava into a **hepatic vein** safely. The right hepatic branch usually gives the straightest run toward the portal bifurcation for needle puncture. **Wedge venography** puffs contrast that outlines portal branches as a roadmap before the needle advances. A curved **Colapinto needle** passes from hepatic vein toward portal bifurcation under careful biplane guidance in theatre.
steps.say: Technique starts at the neck because jugular access gives a straight highway toward the liver veins. Right jugular access under ultrasound guides a sheath down the cava into a hepatic vein. The right hepatic branch usually gives the straightest run toward the portal bifurcation for puncture. Wedge contrast is injected so it outlines portal branches as a roadmap before the needle advances. A curved needle passes from hepatic vein toward portal bifurcation under careful guidance.

steps.tx: This fluoroscopy image is helpful because it shows a sheath that travels from the **right internal jugular vein** down the cava into the **right hepatic vein**. A wedged injection outlines the portal bifurcation as a roadmap, while the curved needle marks the planned **puncture path** through liver tissue. Safe shunt creation depends on access, roadmap and controlled puncture in order. A trainee who follows the labels can reconstruct each step before deployment. Pressure measurement then confirms whether the channel truly decompresses the portal system.
steps.say: This fluoroscopy image is helpful because it shows a sheath that travels from the right neck vein into the right hepatic vein. steps.tx: Pressure measurement decides dilatation endpoints during shunt creation, because gradient predicts clinical benefit afterwards. The **portosystemic gradient** measured before and after sets a target below **12 mmHg** for bleeding control. A **covered stent graft** lines the parenchymal tract and cuts dysfunction compared with bare metal in follow up. **Balloon dilatation** opens the tract stepwise, while an oversized balloon tears the capsule and causes bleeding. Variceal embolisation alongside coils a bleeding coronary vein that a shunt alone may not still completely.

steps.tx: Puncture bleeding declares quickly during shunt creation, so the team watches pressure and contrast spread continuously. **Capsular transgression** spills contrast outside the liver with falling pressure and demands covered extension or embolisation urgently. A crossed bile duct creates a **biliary fistula** that declares with fever and needs antibiotics with drainage. **Arterial injury** beside the tract shows as a blush that the operator treats with coils promptly. A **stent malposition** toward cava or atrium needs pullback or extension under close cardiac watching in theatre.

steps.tx: Patency after shunt creation proves itself on Doppler, because velocity and flow direction reveal stenosis early. **Post TIPS duplex** checks shunt velocity with portal flow direction within days and then at surveillance intervals. Falling velocity with recurrent ascites marks **shunt stenosis** that needs venography with revision in the lab. A **variceal re bleed** after shunting needs remapping that separates shunt failure from varix failure clearly. Lifelong liver follow up continues because a shunt palliates pressure rather than curing cirrhosis itself.
